Centrality values are based on the full network. NA means undefined, not zero. Click table headers to sort.
Definitions, methods, and reproducibility

Degree: number of incident edges; for directed networks, total degree (in + out) is reported. Edge weights are ignored.

Betweenness: fraction of shortest paths passing through a node, excluding endpoints. Normalized as 2B/[(n-1)(n-2)] for undirected networks or B/[(n-1)(n-2)] for directed ones. Defined as zero for n < 3.

Closeness: inverse of the mean distance to reachable nodes, as computed by igraph::closeness(normalized = TRUE). Unreachable nodes are excluded; when no other node is reachable, the result is NA. In disconnected networks, closeness can favor small components and needs cautious interpretation.

Harmonic centrality: sum of reciprocal shortest-path distances divided by n-1. An unreachable node contributes zero. Offered alongside closeness for disconnected networks.

Centrality metrics are computed in R and then embedded in the HTML. Filters affect the display only.

Edge visualization: line thickness is scaled to the magnitude of the original numeric weight attribute within each full network (visual normalization only). Dashed lines indicate negative weights. Hover or click on an edge for the original signed weight. Edge-weight labels and the minimum absolute-weight filter are visualization controls; they never change the original weights. An undefined weight is shown as NA and excluded if a weight threshold is active.

Weights for shortest paths: in unweighted each edge counts as one step. distance uses positive weights already representing distances. inverse_strength uses distance = 1/weight and requires strictly positive weights; this is an explicit modeling choice, not a universal transform for correlations.

Layout: initial coordinates are computed in R using the unweighted Fruchterman–Reingold layout. Dragging nodes or changing layout does not modify the original graph or its centrality scores.

Comparing networks: normalization does not remove differences in network size, density, or connected components. This explorer does not test biological significance.

Sharing: the standalone HTML contains every node and edge, including those hidden by filters. Filtering does not anonymize or remove data. No external resources are loaded.

References: official igraph documentation for degree, betweenness, closeness, harmonic_centrality, and layout_with_fr. See README.md for details.

How to use the explorer

1. Use the Level 1 or Level 2 dropdown to choose a network. All networks share the same interactive graph area.

2. Choose a metric to rank genes and size nodes. Enter 20 under “Show top N genes” to inspect the 20 highest-ranked genes.

3. Enable one or more minimum thresholds. Moving a slider activates its filter. Filters are combined with AND. Missing values are excluded only when their corresponding filter is active; Top N excludes missing values for the selected ranking metric.

4. Search is case-insensitive and accepts partial gene names or multiple genes separated by commas, spaces, or semicolons. Enable “Show only matching genes” to turn search into a filter.

5. Line width reflects absolute edge weights. Hover over or click an edge for its exact signed weight. Use Edge weight labels to display weights on selected or all edges, and filter interactions by minimum absolute weight. Click a node to see its centrality values. “Selected gene + visible neighbors” shows its first-order neighborhood without restoring genes excluded by other filters.

6. Export visible genes or edges as CSV and the graph as SVG. “Save standalone HTML” stores all networks and preserves the current view settings, not only the displayed subgraph.

To share: share the generated HTML file (optionally in a ZIP). Recipients can open the downloaded file in a modern browser without R, Shiny, internet access, or the .rds source files.
